# @mintlify/package-builder

Builds npm package islands for docs that set a `packages` key in docs.json. The same code runs in the Cloudflare Sandbox build container and in `mint dev`.

`packages.isolation: "frame"` is not implemented yet. A build that sets it fails with `isolation-frame-not-implemented` instead of running the islands in the page.

Steps:

1. Validates the lockfile (`package-lock.json` v2/v3 or `pnpm-lock.yaml` v9, which pnpm 9 and 10 write; the build worker reads no other pnpm format): every entry needs `integrity`, and every npm entry except bundled ones needs `resolved` (npm leaves it out under `omit-lockfile-registry-resolved`); `git`, `file:`, `link:` and `http:` sources are rejected; https URLs must be on registry.npmjs.org or on the scope's registry from `packages.registries`. A registry in `packages.registries` must be one the build worker can reach: no port other than 443, no IP address, a host name with a dot, and nothing under `localhost`, `local`, `internal`, `home.arpa`, `cloudflare.com`, `cloudflarestorage.com`, `r2.dev`, `workers.dev` or `pages.dev`. The worker also refuses Mintlify's own domains; that list lives in the server and is not repeated here. package.json dependencies, `overrides` and `pnpm` overrides/extensions must be registry versions, ranges or dist-tags (no `npm:` aliases, git, `file:`, `link:`, `workspace:`, `catalog:`, URLs or paths), `pnpm.patchedDependencies` is rejected, and the lockfile root must match package.json. npm entries marked `inBundle` cannot carry their own `resolved`, and pnpm resolutions may only have `integrity` and `tarball`. For `npm-ci` and `prepared`, package.json and the lockfile must be regular files, not symbolic links, and parse errors report only a line and column.
2. Installs. `npm-ci` copies only package.json and the lockfile into a temp dir, writes its own `.npmrc` (deleted as soon as the install exits, since it can hold registry tokens; registries and tokens containing `${` are rejected because npm fills them from environment variables) and runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev`. It retries once with `--legacy-peer-deps` on ERESOLVE. On Windows it never spawns a `.cmd` shim or a shell: it runs `npm-cli.js` (or pnpm's `pnpm.cjs`/`pnpm.mjs`/`pnpm.js`) with the current Node, or `pnpm.exe`, found from `npm_execpath`, PATH or the Node install, and fails with `package-manager-missing` otherwise. `local` (for `mint dev`) uses the docs folder's existing node_modules and turns lockfile, package.json and registry host errors into warnings. `prepared` is for a caller that installed packages itself, like the build worker: it uses the existing node_modules but keeps every check an error, including installed versions that differ from the lockfile, and never reads node_modules folders above the docs folder. The copied package.json drops `packageManager` and `devEngines`, Corepack is told not to switch versions, and pnpm runs with `package-import-method=copy`; `packageManagers.pnpm` maps a pnpm major to an installed binary, so a project asking for that major gets it and any other major gets the default pnpm with a warning. `registryTokens` is keyed by registry URL: a token is written only for scopes whose registry in `packages.registries` is that URL. `npm-ci` and `prepared` builds reject hard-linked files in packages and docs files.
3. Bundles every island in one esbuild build with code splitting. Imports cannot leave the docs folder or climb out of a package with `..`, `packages.css` entries must be package paths, and `packages.provider` must be a docs path that starts with `/`, such as `/snippets/provider.jsx` (without the `/` the entry would import it as an npm package). A docs or island `import()`/`require()` that builds a `./`, `../` or `/` path at runtime (a template literal with `${}` or string concatenation) fails with `import-runtime-path` before installing, because only statically imported docs files are hashed and copied; dynamic imports of package paths are left alone. Snippets and the provider cannot import a package manager file at the docs root (`package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.pnpmfile.cjs`, `.pnpmfile.mjs`, `yarn.lock`, `.yarnrc`, `.yarnrc.yml`) or any `.npmrc`, because the build worker rejects jobs that send them (`local-file-package-manager`, a warning in `local`); `package.json` can still be imported. Every file esbuild reads, from any importer (packages, their CSS `@import` and `url()`, glob imports, asset loaders), must have a real path (links and Windows 8.3 short names resolved on both sides, compared case-insensitively on Windows) inside the install root's node_modules, the job's docs files or the builder runtime, so a package or a symlink cannot pull in other files; `local` also accepts node_modules folders above the docs folder, where workspaces hoist packages. The metafile is checked again before anything is written. `react`, `react-dom` and their subpaths are aliased to the project's single copy. A separate Node build is used for server rendering.
4. Renders each island in its own child process with `renderToString`, using `identifierPrefix: mi-<id>-` and a 3 s timeout per island, then sanitizes the HTML (256 KB cap). A fresh process per island means module-level counters (lodash `uniqueId`, recharts clip paths, react-select instance ids) start over for every island, so two islands on a page could render the same ids. When the HTML has an `id`, the process renders the island a second time; every id that differs between the two renders (all ids when the second render throws or runs out of time) becomes `mi-<island id>-<old id>`, together with its references in `url(#...)` values, `href`/`xlink:href="#..."` and id-list attributes such as `for` and `aria-labelledby`. Ids from `useId` already carry the prefix, and ids that are the same in both renders, such as a gradient id written in the source, keep their names, so elements React mounts after hydration still find them. React keeps server attributes when it hydrates, so renamed ids stay in the page; the browser's own counter ids never collide with them. Code that runs after hydration only knows the browser's counter values, so an element mounted later that points at a renamed id (a recharts `ReferenceArea` with `ifOverflow="hidden"` shown after load) or a `getElementById` call for one finds nothing; without renaming, that only worked in the first island to hydrate. Islands render one at a time and a process only ever loads one island, so its code can only affect its own result. The parent accepts `start` and then one well-formed `done` (followed by the HTML and the second render's HTML or `null`) or `error` for that island's id, then kills the process; any other message fails that island, except that a malformed or oversized message after the HTML only drops the second render. On Node 20+ the render process runs under `--permission` with read access only to the server bundle and the render script, so an island cannot read other files, write to disk (including rewriting another island's bundle), or spawn a process or worker while it renders. On Windows the builder first renders a probe island under the same flags and drops them if it fails, so a Node permission model that rejects Windows paths degrades to an unsandboxed render instead of failing every island. Results come back as JSON lines on a plain pipe that the parent parses itself, capped at 1M characters per message and 16M characters of HTML, with log entries clipped to 20 of 2,000 characters, and each island's HTML is sanitized before the next island renders, so the builder holds one raw result at a time; Node IPC is not used because its own message handling throws in the parent on crafted input. Anything an island writes to the pipe fails only that island rather than crashing the build. Network egress is not restricted here; the build container blocks it at the container layer, and `mint dev` / `mint packages check` run the project's own code on the developer's machine. `node:sqlite`, which the permission model does not cover, is turned off with `--no-experimental-sqlite`. On Linux the parent stops a render whose resident memory passes `renderMemoryLimitBytes` (2 GiB by default). `npm-ci` and `prepared` builds never render without the permission model; `local` builds warn and render. An island that throws, times out, runs out of memory or cannot be sandboxed is reported as a warning and renders in the browser only.
5. Writes `manifest.json` with sha384 integrity and gzip sizes.

## Shared helpers

Use the focused entry points to share build fingerprints, HTML sanitization and types with hosted services:

```ts
import {
  computeBuildId,
  computeDepsHash,
  computeIslandsHash,
} from '@mintlify/package-builder/hashing';
import {
  MAX_CLIENT_FILE_BYTES,
  MAX_CLIENT_FILES,
  MAX_CLIENT_TOTAL_BYTES,
} from '@mintlify/package-builder/limits';
import { MAX_ISLAND_HTML_BYTES, sanitizeIslandHtml } from '@mintlify/package-builder/sanitize';
import type {
  IslandSpec,
  PackageBuildManifest,
  PackagesConfig,
} from '@mintlify/package-builder/types';
```

The limits entry point has no runtime imports. The sanitizer entry point uses `entities/decode` and standard JavaScript APIs. The hashing entry point uses `node:crypto` and `node:zlib`, so Cloudflare Workers consuming it need `nodejs_compat`. These imports avoid loading the build, installation, bundling and rendering modules exported by the package root. Type-only imports do not load runtime code.

Pin the helper dependency and the build container to the same published package version. A hosted service must still validate and sanitize untrusted container output before publishing it, even when both use the same implementation.

The root import, CLI and existing `@mintlify/package-builder/dist/*` imports remain available. The server and Worker can migrate their copied helpers to these entry points after the package is published.

## Build hashes

`computeDepsHash` and `computeIslandsHash` in `src/hashing.ts` are the one definition of the build keys. The server and the package-builder worker carry ports, and all three must pass `__test__/fixtures/hash-vectors.json` (copied byte for byte into both server tests).

```
H(x)        = lowercase hex sha256 of x (strings as UTF-8)
canonical() = JSON, no whitespace, object keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, undefined keys dropped
depsHash    = H(canonical({ algorithm: 'mint-pkg-deps/1', builderVersion, lockfileKind,
                            lockfile: H(lockfileBytes), dependencies, registries ?? {} }))
islandsHash = H(canonical({ algorithm: 'mint-pkg-islands/1',
                            islands: [{ id, kind, module: H(module) }] sorted by id,
                            snippets: { [path]: H(source) }, provider ?? null, css ?? [],
                            ssr ?? true, isolation ?? 'page' }))
buildId     = H(depsHash + islandsHash).slice(0, 32)
```

`snippets` holds the job's `snippetFiles` plus every docs file that they, `packages.provider` or an island reach through relative or `/` imports, read from `docsRoot` (`collectLocalFiles`). The bundle reads docs files only from that set, so editing an imported helper, JSON or CSS file always changes the hash. A job that already sends every imported file, as the server does, gets the same hash. A `snippetFiles` string is hashed and bundled as its UTF-8 bytes, so it must be the file's exact text, byte order mark and CRLF line endings included. A file whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 (images, fonts, Latin-1 or UTF-16 text) stays out of `snippetFiles` and is read from `docsRoot` as bytes. The server splits files that way: text whose bytes survive a UTF-8 round trip goes in `snippetFiles`, everything else in `assetFiles`, which the worker writes into the docs folder.

A build job can pass `expected: { depsHash, islandsHash }`. The manifest then carries those values, and the build fails with `deps-hash-mismatch` or `islands-hash-mismatch` if the builder computes different ones, so a job keyed under one hash never publishes output built from different inputs.

## Lockfile vectors

The build worker checks lockfiles with its own parser. `__test__/fixtures/lockfile-vectors.json` lists lockfiles and `packages.registries` values with the verdict both must reach: `ok: true` means `validateRegistries`, `validateRegistryHosts` and `validateLockfile` report no error here and the worker's `parseLockfile` succeeds. Error codes differ, so only the verdict is shared. Copy the file byte for byte into the worker's tests, as with `hash-vectors.json`.

## CLI

```sh
mint-package-builder build --input input.json --out dist [--installer local|npm-ci|prepared] [--json]
```

`input.json` is a `BuildInput` without `outDir`. The exit code is 1 when the build has errors.

## Output

```
<out>/manifest.json
<out>/client/islands/<id>.js   exports hydrate(el, { identifierPrefix, props?, theme? })
<out>/client/*.js              shared chunks, one React
<out>/client/styles.css        packages.css plus CSS imported by the provider
<out>/client/styles/<id>.css   CSS imported by one island
<out>/client/assets/<hash>.*   images and fonts, named by content
<out>/server/                  server build (not served)
```

The build fails with `client-too-many-files` above 1,000 client files, `client-file-too-large` for a client file over 8 MB, `client-output-too-large` above 40 MB of client files and `client-bundle-too-large` above 5 MB gzipped. The first three are the hosted build worker's output limits, so `mint dev` reports a package that would fail to deploy. A package entry that lazy-loads a whole set of modules with `import()`, such as a dynamic icon map, emits one file per module and can go over the file limit.

`manifest.css` lists the global `styles.css`, with `packages.css` entries in docs.json order followed by CSS imported by `packages.provider`. Each `manifest.islands[id].css` lists that island's stylesheet. Island styles are walked depth first in the order esbuild uses for CSS imported from JS (static imports in source order, then `import()` and `require()`). Each island keeps its own import order, and omits styles already loaded by the global stylesheet. A package `import()` or `require()` whose path is built at runtime, such as ``import(`./themes/${name}.css`)``, adds every file it matches at its place, sorted by path as esbuild sorts them, and JS files it matches are walked the same way. A `?query` or `#hash` suffix on a stylesheet import is dropped, and an import such as `./button.css` that resolves to a JS file (`button.css.js`) stays JS. Repeated JS imports keep their first place; repeated CSS `@import`s keep their last place, as in esbuild and the browser. A stylesheet that JS loads in a way the walk cannot place, such as a runtime path that matches a symlink to a file elsewhere in the package, fails the build with `css-not-collected`. CSS modules (`.module.css`) fail the build too, whether JS imports them (including code that only the server build loads), a stylesheet `@import`s them or `packages.css` lists them, since the manifest loads plain CSS and cannot map the generated class names. A stylesheet that loads a remote URL (an `@import`, `url()` or `image-set()` string starting with `//` or a scheme other than `data:`) fails the build with `css-remote-url`, so a package cannot keep a stylesheet, font or image on a host it controls. `data:` URLs, `#fragment` references and `@namespace` URIs are kept. Each emitted stylesheet is scanned with the browser's CSS tokenizer rules, so a malformed string or `url()` cannot hide a later URL from the scan.

`manifest.clientAccess` has `{ version: 1, files: { [clientPath]: islandIds }, globalFiles }`. Every file in `manifest.files` has an entry. An island owns its entry, every nonexternal static or dynamic output import, and its stylesheet and CSS assets. Files shared by several islands have all those owners, including identical assets emitted from separate builds. Each island entry has only its own owner. Only the output closure of the explicit global stylesheet is in `globalFiles`; an empty owner list does not imply public access. Hosted serving must keep this immutable map outside the served client directory and authorize each requested artifact using its owners or explicit global status.

JavaScript imports of images and fonts resolve their hashed file-loader paths against `import.meta.url`, keeping the page namespace in the resulting root-relative URL. The server build emits the internal `/_mintlify/pkg-asset/assets/<hash>.<ext>` marker instead. The page compiler replaces that prefix with the page-scoped package base plus `/client/` before injecting sanitized island HTML. CSS asset URLs remain relative to their stylesheet.

Package snippets can read the docs theme with `import { useMintTheme } from '@mintlify/islands'`.

## React rules

| Check                                                             | Result  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| react and react-dom differ on 19.x, or majors differ              | error   |
| react and react-dom differ on 18.x                                | warning |
| more than one react or react-dom in a bundle                      | error   |
| an island throws, logs an error or times out during SSR           | warning |
| the alias replaced a package's own React                          | warning |
| a peer range excludes the installed React                         | warning |
| `findDOMNode`, `ReactDOM.render` or `.defaultProps =` on React 19 | warning |
